If you'd prefer a refund instead, just reply and I'll process that same day. Thanks for your patience!

incoming_email: I've tried resetting my password three times and I'm still locked out of my account (email: j.torres@fastmail.com). This is urgent, I need to access an invoice today.

offer fallback to get the invoice directly

subject: Wrong item shipped

subject: Product stopped working after 2 weeks
incoming_email: The bluetooth speaker I bought two weeks ago won't turn on anymore. It was working fine and I charged it overnight like normal. Is this covered under warranty?

key_points: confirm it is covered under warranty

subject: Subscription charged twice this month
incoming_email: Hi, I just noticed I was charged for my monthly subscription twice this month (once on the 1st and again on the 14th). Can you refund the duplicate charge? My account email is dana.k@webmail.com.

I checked the account under dana.k@webmail.com and confirmed the duplicate charge from the 14th - I've refunded it and you should see it back on your statement within 3-5 business days. I also flagged the billing system so this doesn't happen again next cycle.

give a timeframe for the refund

subject: Pricing for team plan
incoming_email: Hi, we're a 12-person startup interested in your team plan. Could you send pricing and whether there's a discount for annual billing?
reference_reply: Hi, thanks for reaching out! For a 12-person team, our Team plan is $18/user/month billed monthly, or $180/user/year if you go annual - that works out to a 2-month discount. I'm happy to set up a 14-day trial so your team can test it before committing. Want me to spin that up?
key_points: offer a trial or next step

subject: Does your product integrate with Salesforce?
incoming_email: Before we move forward, we need to confirm: does your platform have a native Salesforce integration, or would we need a third-party connector?
reference_reply: Great question - yes, we have a native two-way Salesforce integration (syncs contacts, deals, and activity logs) included on our Growth plan and above, no third-party connector needed. Setup usually takes under 30 minutes with our onboarding team. Happy to do a quick screen-share demo if that would help move the decision along.

subject: Bulk discount for 50 licenses
incoming_email: We're considering purchasing 50 licenses for our department. Is there a volume discount available at that quantity?
reference_reply: Yes - at 50 licenses you'd qualify for our volume tier, which is 20% off list price, bringing it to $24/license/month instead of $30. I can also lock in that rate for a 2-year term if that's useful for budgeting. Want me to draft a formal quote you can share internally?
key_points: offer to draft a formal quote

subject: Trial extension request
incoming_email: Our trial ends Friday but our procurement review got delayed. Any chance we can get a 2-week extension?
reference_reply: No problem at all - I've extended your trial by 2 weeks, so it now runs through the following Friday. That should give procurement the time they need. Let me know if there's anything I can send over to help speed up their review, like a security or compliance packet.

subject: Comparison vs a competitor
incoming_email: We're also evaluating [Competitor X]. What would you say is the main reason to pick your product over theirs, especially for a 30-person marketing team?
reference_reply: Fair question - for a 30-person marketing team, the two things teams usually tell us tip the decision our way are faster onboarding (most teams are live in under a week vs. their typical 3-4 week rollout) and native reporting dashboards, which Competitor X charges extra for as an add-on. Happy to send a side-by-side comparison sheet, or set up a call with one of our marketing-team customers if that would help.
key_points: give at least one concrete differentiator
tie the answer to the marketing team use case
offer supporting evidence or next step

subject: Reschedule Thursday's call
incoming_email: Something came up and I can't make our 2pm call on Thursday. Could we move it to Friday morning instead?
reference_reply: No worries at all - Friday morning works for me. Does 10am Friday suit you? If so I'll send an updated invite; if not, let me know a couple of times that work and I'll match one.
key_points: propose or confirm a specific new time

subject: Finding a time for a 3-way sync
incoming_email: Can we get you, me, and Priya on a call sometime next week to align on the launch timeline? I'm flexible except Monday.
reference_reply: Works for me - I'm open Tuesday afternoon or Wednesday morning next week. I'll loop in Priya and propose Wednesday 10am as a first option, with Tuesday 2pm as backup, and send a poll if neither lands for everyone.
key_points: mention coordinating with the third person

subject: Interview scheduling
incoming_email: Following up from HR - could we set up your interview with the candidate for early next week? They're available Mon-Wed afternoons.
reference_reply: Thanks for the update - Tuesday at 2pm or Wednesday at 3pm both work well on my end. Let's go with Tuesday 2pm if the candidate is fine with that; otherwise Wednesday 3pm is my backup. Happy to hop on a quick 30-minute slot either day.

subject: Client wants to move up the kickoff
incoming_email: The client asked if we can move the project kickoff from next Wednesday to this Friday instead - is that feasible on your end?
reference_reply: Friday works for me, assuming the deck and requirements doc are ready by Thursday EOD - can you confirm that's on track? If so, I'll block Friday 11am and send the updated calendar invite to everyone today.

subject: Doctor's appointment conflicts with team meeting
incoming_email: I have a doctor's appointment during our usual Tuesday 9am standup this week. Can we either move the standup or is it fine if I just catch up on notes after?
reference_reply: Totally fine either way, but let's just move it this week so you don't miss anything live - how does 11am Tuesday work instead? If that's tricky given the appointment, catching up on the notes afterward is genuinely fine too, just let me know which you'd prefer and I'll adjust the invite.
key_points: give the person the choice / flexibility
commit to updating the invite if moved

subject: Question about an unexpected line item
incoming_email: My latest invoice has a $49 'overage fee' I don't recognize. Can you explain what that's for?
reference_reply: Good question - that $49 overage fee is for exceeding your plan's 10,000 API call limit last month; your account used about 12,400 calls. I can walk you through upgrading to a higher tier to avoid this going forward, or if this was a one-time spike, I'm happy to waive this instance as a courtesy. Which would you prefer?
key_points: explain what the charge is for
offer a path to avoid it in future
offer a resolution like a waiver or upgrade

subject: Requesting a formal invoice with our tax ID
incoming_email: Could you reissue our last invoice with our company's tax ID included? Accounting needs it for their records. Tax ID: 84-2210xxx.
reference_reply: Of course - I've updated our records with tax ID 84-2210xxx and reissued the last invoice with it included. You'll find it attached to this email, and all future invoices will automatically include it going forward.

reissue or attach the corrected invoice
confirm future invoices will reflect it

subject: Switching from monthly to annual billing
incoming_email: We'd like to switch our plan from monthly to annual billing to get the discount. What's the process, and will we be charged again right away?
reference_reply: Happy to switch you over - the annual discount brings your rate down by about 17%. When we make the switch, we'll prorate your remaining monthly balance against the annual charge, so you won't be double-billed; you'll just see one adjusted charge reflecting the difference. I can process this today if you confirm you'd like to proceed.
key_points: explain how proration/billing will work (no double charge)

subject: Card declined, need to update payment method
incoming_email: I got a notice that my card on file was declined. I have a new card - how do I update it before my account gets suspended?
reference_reply: No problem, and good news - your account won't be suspended for a few more days, so there's time. You can update your card directly under Billing > Payment Methods in your account settings; once the new card is saved, I'll manually retry the failed charge right away so nothing gets interrupted.
key_points: explain how to update the payment method
offer to retry the charge once updated

subject: Refund request after cancelling mid-cycle
incoming_email: I cancelled my subscription on the 5th but was billed for the full month on the 1st. Can I get a prorated refund for the unused days?
reference_reply: Thanks for reaching out, and sorry for the confusion. Since you cancelled on the 5th, you're entitled to a prorated refund for the remaining 26 days of that billing cycle - that comes to about $38.50 based on your plan rate, which I've refunded to your original payment method. It should land within 3-5 business days.
key_points: confirm eligibility for a prorated refund
state or estimate the refund amount
give a timeframe for it to appear

subject: Extremely disappointed - third support ticket ignored
incoming_email: This is my THIRD email about the same login bug and nobody has responded in over a week. I'm seriously considering cancelling. This is unacceptable.
reference_reply: You're right to be frustrated, and I'm sorry this has dragged on for a week with no update - that's not the experience we want you to have. I've escalated your login bug directly to our engineering lead as a priority ticket, and I'll personally follow up with a real update within 24 hours, not another form response. I'd also like to offer a service credit for the trouble this has caused.
key_points: acknowledge the frustration without being defensive
commit to a concrete follow-up timeframe
offer some form of goodwill gesture

subject: Delivery 2 weeks late with no communication
incoming_email: My order was supposed to arrive two weeks ago. I've heard nothing from anyone. I want to know exactly what happened and what you're going to do about it.
reference_reply: I completely understand the frustration - two weeks with no update is well below what you should expect from us, and I'm sorry. Looking into it, your order was held up at a regional carrier facility; it's now been re-routed and is scheduled to arrive within 3 business days. I've also applied a refund of your shipping cost for the delay. I'll personally track this until it arrives.
key_points: acknowledge and apologize for the delay
give a concrete new arrival estimate
offer compensation like a shipping refund

subject: Rude support interaction
incoming_email: The agent I spoke to yesterday was dismissive and talked over me the entire call. I didn't even get my question answered. I want this looked into.
reference_reply: I'm sorry to hear that - that's not the standard we hold our team to, and I appreciate you telling me directly. I'll be reviewing the call with the team lead to address it. In the meantime, let's make sure your original question actually gets answered - can you tell me again what you needed, and I'll personally see it through this time?

subject: Charged after cancelling account entirely
incoming_email: I cancelled my account two months ago and just got charged again. This is the second time this has happened. I want a full refund and confirmation this is actually cancelled.
reference_reply: I'm sorry - this should not have happened a second time, and I understand why that's alarming. I've confirmed your account is now fully cancelled and closed, refunded both incorrect charges in full (you'll see them back within 3-5 business days), and flagged your account so no further charges can be processed. I'd also like to send written confirmation once the refund clears so you have it on record.
key_points: apologize and acknowledge the repeat failure
confirm the account is actually cancelled
prevent recurrence and offer written confirmation

subject: Product safety concern
incoming_email: I need to flag something serious: the phone charger I bought from you got noticeably hot and started smelling like burning plastic after 10 minutes of use. I unplugged it immediately. This seems like a real safety hazard and I want to know what you're doing about it.
reference_reply: Thank you for reporting this right away and for unplugging it immediately - that was the right call. This is a serious safety concern and I'm treating it as one: please stop using the charger entirely, and I'm sending a prepaid return label so we can inspect the unit and check it against other units from the same batch. I'm also issuing a full refund now, independent of the return, and flagging this internally with our product safety team today.
key_points: take the safety concern seriously, not dismissively
instruct the user to stop using the product
arrange to get the unit back for inspection
mention internal escalation to the right team

subject: Requesting better payment terms
incoming_email: As we renew this year, we'd like to move from Net 30 to Net 60 payment terms given the size of our order. Is that something you can accommodate?
reference_reply: Thanks for raising this ahead of renewal. Net 60 is a bigger shift than we typically offer, but given your order volume, I can offer Net 45 as a middle ground, which I'm able to approve without further sign-off. If Net 60 is a hard requirement, I'd need to check with finance, but I wanted to give you a fast answer on what I can commit to today.
key_points: offer a concrete counter or alternative
be transparent about what needs further approval
keep tone collaborative, not just a flat no

subject: Asking for a price hold on renewal
incoming_email: We noticed pricing has gone up 15% since we signed last year. Given we're renewing for another 2 years, could you hold last year's pricing?
reference_reply: I appreciate you bringing this up directly. A full price hold isn't something I can approve, but for a 2-year renewal I can cap the increase at 5% instead of the standard 15%, and lock that rate for the full term so you're protected from further increases. Let me know if that works and I'll get the paperwork moving.
key_points: respond to the price hold request specifically
tie the offer to the multi-year commitment
invite the client to confirm and move forward

subject: Requesting an SLA amendment
incoming_email: Our legal team wants the SLA response-time guarantee tightened from 24 hours to 8 hours for critical issues before we sign. Can you accommodate this?
reference_reply: That's a reasonable ask given how critical issues are for your team - I can commit to an 8-hour response guarantee specifically for issues classified as critical severity, while keeping 24 hours for standard priority items. I'll get the amended SLA language drafted and sent to your legal team by end of week.
key_points: commit to a concrete next step (drafting amendment)

subject: Vendor pushing back on our proposed discount
incoming_email: We understand you're asking for a 25% volume discount, but that's beyond what we can offer given current margins. We can go to 12%. Let us know if that works or if there's room to meet in the middle.
reference_reply: Thanks for the transparency on margins - 12% is a bit lower than we were hoping for, but I understand the constraint. Would 18% work if we commit to a 3-year term instead of 1-year? That gives you more predictability on your side, which might make the deeper discount easier to justify internally.
key_points: acknowledge the vendor's counter without immediately caving
offer something in exchange (e.g., longer term) to justify it

subject: Supplier flags a raw material cost increase
incoming_email: Due to a rise in raw material costs, we need to increase our unit price from $4.20 to $4.95 starting next quarter. We understand this affects your margins and are open to discussing, but wanted to give you advance notice.
reference_reply: Appreciate the advance notice rather than a surprise mid-quarter change - that genuinely helps us plan. A jump to $4.95 is a meaningful hit on our side though, so before we accept it outright, would you be open to phasing it in - say $4.55 next quarter and $4.95 the quarter after - or discussing a small volume commitment from us in exchange for holding closer to $4.60? Open to a call this week to work through it.
key_points: not simply accept the full increase without pushback
propose a specific alternative (phasing or volume-for-price)
offer to continue the conversation (e.g., a call)
